newsitem.title: USA: NEES sees "intense" bidding for assets.
newsitem.headline: NEES sees "intense" bidding for assets.

text.p: New England Electric System Chief Executive John Rowe said Monday the company's auction of its generating assets is expected to generate "quite intense" competition.
Speaking at a conference on the restructuring in the electric utility industry in New England, Rowe said the auction will "literally cut the company in half."
"I expect, from what we have seen, the competition will be quite intense," he said.

Twenty-five bids have been received for the company's 18 non-nuclear electric generating plants and its purchased power contracts up for sale. NES said an unspecified number of bidders had been invited to prepare more formal bids.
Rowe previously said the company hoped to have a deal to sell the assets early in the third quarter.

NEES is selling 4,000 megawatts of fossil and hydro capacity, including three fossil-fuel plants, a pumped storage hydro plant, and the region's largest renewable portfolio consisting of 14 hydroelectric facilities, as well as 1,500 megawatts of purchased power contracts.
Rowe said today he expected a number of "better bids" would be for the entire fleet of generating assets or for the fossil fuel plants as a group or the hydroelectric plants as a group.
After selling the generating plants, NEES will concentrate on delivering electricity, but will also enter a number of other businesses, he said.
"We intend to have a place in the telecom industry," he said.
NEES may also get involved in the delivery of gas and the transmission of electricity in other states or countries, he said.
